claims: Gary Woodland was the 2019 U.S. Open champion.
Gary Woodland was diagnosed with PTSD following September 2023 brain surgery.
Gary Woodland's September 2023 brain surgery was to remove a tumor.
The tumor caused intense fear and anxiety.
Gary Woodland opened up in March 2026 about struggling with symptoms like hypervigilance, blurry vision, and panic attacks on the course.
Gary Woodland's PTSD stemmed from the traumatic experience of brain surgery.
Gary Woodland's PTSD stemmed from the preceding months of dealing with a lesion.
The lesion was located on a part of the brain controlling fear and anxiety.
Gary Woodland experienced extreme anxiety on the course.
Gary Woodland experienced instances of hypervigilance where he could not have people behind him.
Gary Woodland had blurry vision during tournaments.
Gary Woodland lost focus during tournaments.
For months, Gary Woodland hid his condition.
Gary Woodland cried in scoring trailers.
Gary Woodland ran to his car after rounds.
Gary Woodland admitted that despite returning to golf, he felt like he was "living a lie".
Gary Woodland went public with his PTSD diagnosis in March 2026.
Gary Woodland stated, "I can't waste energy anymore hiding this".
Gary Woodland noted that going public felt like a "thousand pounds" off his back.
Doctors suggested Gary Woodland avoid high-stress environments.
Gary Woodland has continued to play golf.
Gary Woodland stated that golf is his dream.
Gary Woodland stated that he will not let the PTSD win.
